sections.overview: ITIS lists this as a valid species of the orthonectid genus Stoecharthrum.
sections.identification: The original description reports specimens 300–365 μm long, with 40–46 epidermal cell rings.
sections.habitat: It was found in Ascidia callosa from floating docks at Roche Harbor, Washington.
sections.reproduction: The original study reports tightly grouped oocytes and sperm or its precursors in some specimens.
sections.ecology: Unlike S. fosterae in Mytilus trossulus, S. burresoni infects an ascidian and is shorter, with fewer cell rings and oocytes.
sections.conservation: No species-level conservation assessment was found; the description is from one locality.
